<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eeaa882459edffd077c1cda2972af06d1f10550b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

git fetch origin 43e8cb08fae61da11006ad3869a40542631f4c73 && git checkout 43e8cb08fae61da11006ad3869a40542631f4c73
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eeaa882459edffd077c1cda2972af06d1f10550b c8665778a20877e7e378d3ea19c63e870180a42b && git checkout -B drift-repro eeaa882459edffd077c1cda2972af06d1f10550b && git merge --no-ff c8665778a20877e7e378d3ea19c63e870180a42b

> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c8665778a20877e7e378d3ea19c63e870180a42b`

Isolated contract review of PR #19183 for card #16292, judged adversarially from the card, its rulings, the PR body, the full diff at the head above, and the tree at `origin/main` (`eeaa882459`). Seat comments and the `os-dev-report` were read as assertions and re-measured; nothing below is adopted from them.

**Authority relied on.** Director-seat ruling on the card, comment 5594059768, read at 2026-09-09T00:50Z: "the carrier is hung only with a reviewable increment — a draft PR, or the card in the same stroke as a `Clause-②: yes` claim — and a triage verdict records the clause-② direction in prose. Triage's direction (narrowing what `defineJob` accepts on a published schema — declare it at claim time) stays on this thread; the claim that takes this card decides the declaration and re-hangs the carrier if `yes`." The triage comment 5579723860 is not a ruling (the seat says so itself); its ICU fence is treated below as a direction I re-measured, not as authority.

### ① Derived judgments

The card's direction is a narrowing of what a published schema accepts. The diff does exactly that and nothing wider. Item by item:

1. **`CronScheduleSchema.timezone` — `z.string()` becomes `z.string().refine(isValueDomainMember('iana_time_zone', …))`** (`packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts`). Accept set narrows from "any string" to "strings the host's `Intl.DateTimeFormat` constructs". Implementer's classification (narrowing, no new key/member/export): **right.** Reach, measured: `CronScheduleSchema`, the cron arm of `ScheduleSchema`, `JobSchema.schedule`, `defineJob`, and the seven published artifacts that embed a job manifest (the ledger's new rows). Base premise re-read: `origin/main:packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts:17` was still the bare string.
   - Tests at head: `src/system/job.test.ts` + `src/shared/value-domain.test.ts` run by me on this container — 77 passed (77), exit 0.
   - Predicate re-probed on Node v22.22.2 / ICU 78.2 / tz 2025c / full-icu: MEMBER `UTC`, `utc`, `GMT`, `EST5EDT`, `Etc/GMT+8`, `Asia/Kolkata`, `Asia/Calcutta`, `Europe/Kyiv`, `US/Eastern`, `America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires`, `America/Ciudad_Juarez`, `europe/zurich`; REFUSED `UTC+8`, `GMT+8`, `Z`, `Local`, `Europe/Munich`, `China Standard Time`, `Asia/Shanghai ` (trailing space), `` (empty), `not a zone`. `Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone')` has 418 entries and omits `UTC` and `Asia/Kolkata` — the test docblock's claim holds on this host.
   - Runtime parity, read from `node_modules/.pnpm/croner@10.0.1/…/dist/croner.js`: croner judges the zone by the same `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone })` construction (its `toTZ` helper throws `RangeError` on failure). On one host the parse-time set and the schedule-time set are therefore the same set by construction; no value croner honours is refused at parse on the same host.
   - Runtime boot does not re-parse: nothing in `packages/runtime/src` calls `JobSchema.parse` (grep); `app-plugin.ts` lowers through `toBoundaryJobSchedule`. The narrowing bites at `defineJob` (module import), `os build` (`ManifestSchema.safeParse`, `packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/build.ts:111`) and `os validate` — the authoring tier the card names. Consequence worth stating plainly: because `defineJob` runs at import time, an app whose jobs module carries a refused zone now fails to start rather than logging one `FAILED TO SCHEDULE` — that is the card's declared intended direction ("stops BUILDING instead of booting-and-not-running") and the triage seat's reading, and that job never ran anyway.
   - **One exclusion the PR prose does not discuss, named here: the empty string.** At base `timezone: ''` parsed; at runtime `timezoneOf` (`packages/runtime/src/job-schedule.ts:101-103`) drops `''`, and `CronJobAdapter` then applies its `defaultTimezone` of `'UTC'` (`packages/services/service-job/src/cron-job-adapter.ts:99,132`). So a job authored with `''` built, booted and ran — in UTC, by fall-through. It is now refused at parse with a message that names `'UTC'` as the fix. Judgment: **correctly refused.** `''` was never a contract value — the published doc already says "`timezone` is an IANA name and defaults to `UTC`" (`content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx:119`) — and a wrong value silently coerced to the default is precisely the class the north star refuses. It is not a value a deployment legitimately honoured; the deployment honoured "absent". It does, however, falsify one sentence of the changeset (see ②).
   - Offset spellings `+08:00` / `-05:00` are MEMBERS on this host (ECMA-402 offset time zones) although they are not IANA identifiers. This is a pre-existing property of the `iana_time_zone` domain (its definition is the probe, per the module header of `value-domain.zod.ts`), not something this diff introduces; croner honours them through the same constructor. The new `.describe()` and error text say "a UTC offset such as `UTC+8` is not one", which is literally true and does not claim every offset spelling is refused. Recorded so that "IANA" is not read as stricter than the domain actually is; not a fault of this PR.
   - No in-tree producer of a now-refused value: `examples/app-showcase` writes `timezone: 'UTC'`; docs examples write `UTC` / `America/New_York`; the console preview samples write `UTC`; objectui's `JobPreview` only renders; `metadata-form-registry.ts` has no job form that could emit `''`.
2. **`.describe()` text on the same key** — reaches the published JSON Schema `description` and the generated reference `content/docs/references/system/job.mdx` (three tables). Documentation surface, not accept/reject. Implementer's classification (mandatory regenerated consequence): **right.** Re-generated by me at head with `gen:docs`: the tree stays clean, so the committed `.mdx` is exactly what the generator emits.
3. **`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`** — +3 published schemas (200→203), +7 sites (551→558): `system/CronSchedule`, `system/Job`, `system/Schedule`, and the four `api/*` envelopes that embed `manifest.jobs`. Verified by running `gen:schema` at head: exit 0, and it prints "558 refinement site(s) across 203 published schema(s) … all declared". The published `json-schema/system/CronSchedule.json` now carries `x-dropped-refinements: [{ at: 'timezone', … }]` and its `timezone` property remains `type: string` — the published JSON Schema stays WIDER than the runtime for this key, which is the ledger's declared gap. Could it have been projected instead? The closed list in `src/shared/refinement-projection.ts` has four arms (`required-one-of`, `non-blank-string`, `dependent-required`, `banned-keys`); none can state a host-Intl membership set, and an arm must accept EXACTLY the runtime set — no enum snapshot equals a host-dependent set. Dropped-and-annotated is the only correct route. Classification **right**; the ledger grew for a reason the ledger's own description admits.
4. **Public surface.** `CronTimezoneSchema` is a module-local `const`, not exported; `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json` is untouched (`CronScheduleSchema (const)` unchanged, no new row); no new key, closed-set member, `StandardErrorCode`, or registry row. `scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs --declaration no --diff` on the PR diff: 0 tells on the one contract source file (the changeset, `.mdx`, ledger and test are NOT MEASURED by design). The Zod type of `timezone` is unchanged (`.refine()` keeps `ZodString`), so the `.d.ts` surface does not move. Implementer's "no public-surface change": **right.**
5. **`job.test.ts`** — +5 tests, one of them the corpus-equality invariant against the shared predicate. Correctly pins the schema to the predicate rather than to this container's tz database.
6. **Changeset** — judged in ②.

Does the diff do more than the card's narrowing? **No.** One key's accept set narrows; everything else is the description, the projection ledger, tests and the changeset.

### ② Semver level

- **Level `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`**, the one package whose `src` the diff moves. Read for myself in `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: during the launch window `major` is refused and "breaking changes ship as `minor`"; the stated END CONDITION is that at GA "an accept-set narrowing … grades `major`"; until then "it is NOT the carrier … The mandatory information carriers for breaking-ness in the meantime are the **BREAKING** banner the author writes in the changeset body and the ADR-0087 migration-ledger disposition". The `Check Changeset` prose in `pr-automation.yml` says the same. The changeset carries the `**BREAKING**` banner, the `!` is on the title, and the ADR-0087 marker is present. **Level and breaking-ness declaration agree with what the diff does.**
- **ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.** Run by me at head: `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main --head pr-19183` → exit 0, reading the changeset as `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The category is honest on its own terms: the body carries no FROM → TO prescription, and none exists — an offset spelling names no zone, so nothing mechanical can be applied; a ledger row would carry an empty mapping. Not `already-registered` under `platform-timezone-columns-iana-domain-refused`: agreed, that entry is the column tier, a different door. Same shape as the landed `.changeset/18124-genuine-duration-rows-declare-their-unit.md`.
- **Level axis with the real declaration input**: `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main --head pr-19183 --event` fed the live PR payload → exit 0: "LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② `yes (narrowing)`, and no package whose `packages/**/src/**` it moves is graded `patch`"; "direction arm: `narrowing` — a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships `minor`". CI `Check Changeset` at this head: success (its job log was not fetchable through this session's proxy — the reading above is my own reproduction with the PR's payload). `check-empty-changeset` → exit 0.
- **One inaccuracy in the changeset prose, non-blocking:** "No job that ran yesterday stops running." That is false for exactly one value — `timezone: ''`, which ran in UTC by the runtime's drop-and-default (①.1) and is now refused at parse; because `defineJob` runs at import, the stack carrying it fails to start until the key is deleted or written as `'UTC'`. The refusal text prescribes that fix, and no in-tree producer writes `''`, so this is an overstated CHANGELOG sentence rather than a wrong direction. If the branch moves again for any reason, amend it to say that an empty-string zone, previously dropped and run as UTC, is now refused. Not a patch-round condition on its own.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Should `Clause-②: yes` stand, or be overturned to `no`?** Overturned: the declaration of record is **`no (narrowing)`**. The charter's own reading governs, verbatim from `references/lanes/spec.md`: 「放宽接受集或扩大公开面的卡,不论多小,即条款②;收窄仍是契约面,不触条款②。」 and 「收窄不触发条款②,但按 `yes` 申报恒不是错误;⛔ 个案裁决不改本行。」 Measured against that: no key, member, export, error code or registration is added (①.4, tells 0, `api-surface` untouched, `CronTimezoneSchema` local); the published contract text already declared the domain (`content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx:119`, and the old `.describe()`'s only example is an IANA name), so this is declared ≠ enforced pulled back. The `yes` was the charter-sanctioned conservative direction at claim time and is not a seat fault (「声明被复核推翻 ⛔ 不作席位过失」). Consequence for landing: **none** — every gate that reads the line reads the ARM (level axis enforces `minor` for `yes (narrowing)` and `no (narrowing)` alike; the ADR-0087 gate reads the narrowing arm; `check-clause2-carriers --pair 19183` exits 0 with both carriers hung and judges the declaration limb from the card, treating the PR-body line as input only), and the review this record constitutes is the tier the `yes` routed to, so its routing purpose is discharged. If the branch moves again, align the PR body and the changeset line to `no (narrowing)` as `17499` and `18124` spell it.
2. **ICU / environment sensitivity** (the card's own open question and the triage seat's fence). Re-measured on this container, which is the repo's pinned baseline: Node v22.22.2, ICU 78.2, tz 2025c, full-icu (de-DE month renders "Januar"); the two zones the triage comment named are members, as are `Europe/Kyiv`, `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`, `US/Eastern`, `GMT` and `America/Ciudad_Juarez` (tzdata 2022g). Answer: the accept set is the host's Intl by the `iana_time_zone` domain's own definition (module header of `value-domain.zod.ts`), the same exposure already carried by the four columns, the settings door (`service-settings/src/value-domains.ts`) and `resolveAuthzContext` (`core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:1151`); croner judges by the same constructor, so on one host parse and schedule cannot disagree. Residual, named rather than waved at: a build host whose tzdata is OLDER than the deploy host's can refuse a zone added since — a build-time refusal of a zone the deployment could honour, the direction the card flagged. That residual is loud (a located error with a prescription), bounded by tzdata age rather than ICU size, and is the platform's existing commitment for this concept, not a decision this PR makes. Not measured here: a `small-icu` / `system-icu` Node build (`engines: node >=22` does not by itself pin full-icu). No escalation needed.
3. **Boundary type `JobSchedule.timezone`** (`packages/spec/src/contracts/job-service.ts`) — the triage seat placed it outside this card; the diff leaves it untouched; it is the lowered shape nothing authors directly. Agreed; not part of ①.
4. **`interval` / `once` carry no zone** — confirmed in the schema arms and now pinned by a test at head.
5. **Out-of-scope finding (JobSchema `@example` uses the retired `id`)** — verified at head: the example block in `job.zod.ts` opens with `id: "job_sync_meta"` while the same file's `guidance: { id: JOB_ID_RETIRED }` tombstones that key. Real, source-TSDoc only, correctly left out of this PR; it belongs to the seat's filing.
6. **The report's C1 split carrier** (label on the card, not on the PR at report time) — resolved: `--pair 19183` now exits 0 with `needs:contract-review` read on both carriers.
7. **The adversarial question:** does this change make an invalid value loudly refused at authoring time without making any value a real deployment could honour newly unacceptable? **Yes.** Every refused value either never scheduled (croner refuses it through the same probe) or was the empty string, which was never a contract value and was honoured only as "absent" (①.1). Every zone a deployment honours is a member on that same host.

Checks at this head at judgment time: 37 runs, 0 red; one `Test Core` shard (1/6), `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Type Check · workspace` were still in progress (29 success, 5 skipped) when this record was written — the seat's landing check ③ (all green) is still owed and is not asserted here. Not re-run locally: the full `@objectstack/spec` suite and the consumer-package tests at head.

Reviewed-by: `session_01JbZnqu8bt6YqfJsr9vaFb3` — the seat that adopts this record; rendered by an isolated contract-review subagent, mode:subagent, scratch under pr-19183
